title: Mitigate clock-drift causing DNSSEC validation failures for Private control plane during upgrade
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: During a coordinated control plane upgrade for Private/VPC customers, several control plane nodes experienced transient clock drift after the upgrade leader restarted the system NTP service. The clock skew (up to ~4 minutes on affected hosts) triggered DNSSEC validation failures in our internal resolver chain, causing TLS handshake failures and control-plane RPC timeouts for connected Private agents. Impact: ~12% of Private clusters experienced degraded control plane connectivity for ~27 minutes before rollback and clock resynchronization. Root cause: upgrade sequence restarted chrony/ntpd without waiting for time sync stabilization; an uncommon combination of aggressive DNSSEC validation on the resolver VMs and cached negative responses caused cascading resolver errors.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Incident declared by on-call (Maya P): Multiple Private clusters reporting control plane timeouts and certificate validation errors immediately after control plane upgrade. Pagerduty paged infra and network teams.

2026-03-01 - Initial triage (Liam O'): Observed large negative NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL spikes from internal resolvers correlated with host clock offsets. Suspected time skew + DNSSEC combination. Began rollback of the rolling upgrade to stop further restarts.

2026-03-01 - Mitigation (Infra lead, Chen Z): Rolled back the upgrade in 4 AZs, forced chrony restart with peer and NTP pool fallback, and ran 'chronyc makestep' on impacted hosts. Control plane heartbeats recovered for ~80% of clusters within 27 minutes.

2026-03-02 - Root cause analysis (Maya P): Determined upgrade orchestration restarted time-sync services before verifying time offset < 5s. Internal resolvers validate DNSSEC strictly and reject signatures when local clocks are off by minutes; this produced persistent negative cache entries that affected subsequent lookups.

2026-03-03 - Action plan drafted (Liam O'): 1) Add pre-upgrade time-health check to orchestrator; 2) Make chrony restart idempotent and wait for 'system-clock-synchronized' before proceeding; 3) Add resolver negative-cache short-circuiting post-upgrade; 4) Implement a monitoring alert for host clock drift > 15s; 5) Update runbook for time-sync incidents.
2026-03-03 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/7092 - add time-health gating to upgrade sequencer (reviewers: @chen, @roxanne)
2026-03-04 - PM review (Janelle R): Approved prioritization for P0 mitigations; requested adding canary gating to ensure upgrade sequencer doesn't advance if >1% hosts fail time-health check.

2026-03-04 - Security note (Avery K): Verified DNSSEC policy change scope. We will not relax validation globally; instead we will short-circuit resolver negative cache on affected internal zones for a 5-minute window post-upgrade.
2026-03-05 - Follow-ups scheduled: infra to implement chrony wait + alert (ENG-61301), platform to add resolver cache short-circuit (ENG-61302), QA to add time-drift e2e in staging (ENG-61305).

2026-03-05 - Confluence writeup: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/2026-03-01+Private+Control+Plane+Clock+Drift+Incident - contains timeline, packet captures, and the list of impacted customers (redacted)
